posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
NEVER, EVER modify JSON files in Data folder unless you know exactly
know what your doing, as messing 1 thing up or wrong input make the
other data corrupt as it cannot read them.
MapInfo.json should never be updated, as it mostly update itself when
you add maps to your project and run them.
those files are visible, but if the data is incorrect, it makes the other data
corrupt from reading, so don't touch ANY of the json in data.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Timerox said:
I saved me game moments ago before turning my computer off and on because my internet was unstable.
Click to expand...
The harddrive (like many other computer parts) has its own electronics and RAM, and when Windows gives the order to save data it is written into that RAM before being transferred to the magnetic storage surface of the drive.
The reason for that is because the storage process is much slower than any RAM can ever be - the RAM-Cache speeds up the harddrive a lot.
Unfortunately for you, that is also the reason for the shutdown process of windows - during which windows waits until all hardware reports the "RAM clear" before giving the command to turn off the computer.
Simply cutting power or overriding that shutdown for a faster restart will always contain the risk of losing data, due to interrupting those hardware processes.
Additionally, storing data like your project inside the program folders (especially inside steam folders) has problems of its own - mostly security and access rights problems. It should not be done this way, but the files should be saved elsewhere.

posts.author: firestalker
posts.body:
Code:
$gamePlayer.x === $gameVariables.value(183) && $gamePlayer.y === $gameVariables.value(184)
I have this code snippet that uses game variables to match the event and player together, but I'm not sure if it's what your looking for.
Edit: Nevermind....  I just played around with that code snippet and came up with a much better one that works SOOOO much better and more efficiently:
Place this in the script portion of a conditional branch:
Code:
$gamePlayer.x === $gameMap.event(this._eventId)._realX && $gamePlayer.y === $gameMap.event(this._eventId)._realY

Hey I have a post on this as well and I got some feedback from others if you want to peruse it as well:
RPG Maker MV: "Unable to Read" error. Files corrupting after restarting computer. Help?
[RPG Maker MV] Issue: Unable to Read Game Files issue upon closing RPGMaker MV and restarting PC. I've googled around and found other people having this issue at various times but it seems uncommon so there doesn't seem to be an exact "aha" solution to this problem but this is my issue.  I'm...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
After that conversation here’s what I’m personally doing to avoid this issue from happening now:
+Save Project like normal
+Save a Backup of the project where easily accessible
+Make a backup of the data folder if those files inside of it only are having this issue
+Don't Close RPG Maker with the X but instead: File>Exit RPG Maker (may or may not be needed)
+Allow time for Windows to transfer changes from ram into permanent HDD storage(or whatever)
+If you must turn off computer maybe use the uber slow shut down option from windows menu.
